title: Turnout at Israel's election has reached a record high at the halfway stage
summary: Almost 45% of the electorate had voted by 2 p.m., the highest share since such records began in 1973. The highly anticipated vote is expected to be a close-fought contest, and perhaps even a…

image.caption: Queues stretched out of the doors of some polling stationsImage: Jewel Samad/AFP

blocks.text: WATCH — Author, politician Avraham Burg on why a Palestinian peace process barely featured in the campaign
While security remained the dominant issue for Israeli voters, one topic was largely absent from the election campaign: a peace process with the Palestinians.
After years of conflict and failed negotiations, that debate has been pushed to the political margins.
Has Israeli society abandoned the idea of coexistence?
Avraham Burg, an Israeli writer and former Speaker of the Israeli Parliament, shares his insights with DW.
Israel: No peace vision on the ballot?
